title: Miri Standard Test Patterns
description: Schema for test-patterns.json - how to test an integration against this package, extracted from the package's own test suite

test_framework.description: The framework the package's own suite uses, as evidenced by its test files (e.g. pytest, unittest). Declared so a consumer can match idiom, not as a requirement on the consumer.

supported_test_doubles.description: Fakes, stubs, or fixtures the package SHIPS for consumers to test against. A consumer may rely on these; anything absent here is not a supported double, and a consumer must not present a synthesized one as though it were.

patterns.description: Test patterns, each demonstrating how to test one surface

purpose.description: What this double stands in for, and its fidelity limits

replaces.description: The real surface this double substitutes for

kind.description: unit = the package's surface is exercised in isolation, with doubles for anything external. integration = a real dependency or network endpoint participates.

surface.description: The package surface this pattern tests, named as it appears in sdk-manifest.json api_index

code.description: The test body itself, runnable as written given setup

assertion.description: What the test asserts, if not evident from code

teardown.description: Cleanup required after the test, if any

requires_network.description: Whether running this pattern reaches the network. A consumer MUST treat true as requiring explicit opt-in, since a test suite that silently makes live calls is a supply-chain and cost surprise.

requires_credentials.description: Whether the pattern needs real credentials. A consumer MUST NOT fabricate or substitute credentials to make such a pattern run.

source_file.description: The test file in the package's own suite this pattern was extracted from — evidence, per the Generation Invariants
